label: rem:no-goedel-closed-chains
title: No closed causal chains under the tick definition: the Gödel universe
html:
Take time order to be the order of crossing applications, so one tick is one application of a crossing, as in the proof of (braiding-induced ordering). This is a modelling choice. What follows from it is (crossing-application chains).

Gödel's rotating solution [goedel1949] is homogeneous, and a closed timelike curve passes through every event. Since Gödel's spacetime is connected, this is equivalent to saying that the chronological future I^{+}(p) is all of spacetime for every p.

Under the tick definition there are three cases. On words, for any braiding, no state lies on a closed chain. On a state monoid with a writhe-type degree, a homomorphism to \mathbb{Z} taking every crossing to 1, no state lies on a closed chain either; the braid group B_n is an example. When a crossing has finite order, every state lies on a closed chain; for a symmetric braiding the chain has length two. The statement concerns the tick model only; Gödel's metric remains an exact solution of the Einstein equations.
